title: fix(agents): complete deletion with large idle session histories
body:
Related: #194541

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes agent deletion failing with `worker task capacity reached` when hundreds of idle sessions are stored, and a deleting agent making the whole session catalog unavailable.

## User Impact

Interrupted deletion can complete on restart without flooding the worker pool. Healthy agents remain visible in catalogs while deletion is pending. Offline workspace recovery safeguards and explicit deleted-agent refusals remain intact. No configuration, schema, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Deletion started every stored session drain concurrently, including worker-backed placement checks for idle sessions. The existing concurrency runner now limits that producer to four drains while agent-wide cancellation remains independent. Catalog planning and delivery use the journal's existing deletion fact to omit deleted scopes before explicit database admission.

Production grows by 15 lines: seven to replace eager fan-out with the existing bounded runner and eight to consume the existing catalog exclusion fact. There is no new scheduler, cache, retry policy, or dependency. The 85-line test allocation covers the capacity regression and catalog planning/delivery boundaries.

## Evidence

- Pre-fix: the real Gateway restart regression with 385 stored sessions records `worker task capacity reached` and leaves cleanup incomplete. After the fix it completes cleanup and permits agent recreation. Both deleted-agent catalog regressions also fail on the base and pass here.
- 141 focused tests pass across deletion, active cancellation, restart recovery, offline workspace protection, catalog snapshots/visibility, and mutation/deadline behavior. Final integration file: 98.62 seconds; the active fixture retains its original RPC deadline.
- Codex autoreview is scoped clean through P2 against `4ca233c908c68b9e0e8afb4b83f1f4723d028dc0`. Core and test types, lint, formatting, and import boundaries pass. These server modules are not imported by the Control UI.
- `pnpm check:changed` completed: 34/36 checks pass. The two failed checks and the separate test-line deficit reproduce on the exact parent; attribution is below. No production system was accessed.

Synthetic owner proof used 349 fresh idle sessions per drain, a separate 35.018 GiB keeper database with 10,000 sessions, and a 62,000-file/1.116 GB workspace. Five interleaved pairs plus A/A controls on APFS:

| Metric | Base | Fix |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Completed drains | 0/5 | 5/5 |
| Peak placement-read concurrency | 349 | 4 |
| Overload failures per drain | 41–93 | 0 |
| Median owner wall time | 250.4 ms | 274.5 ms |
| Median host / process CPU | 228.7 / 564.8 ms | 253.7 / 624.8 ms |
| Median sampled allocation (separate pass) | 101.2 MB | 118.0 MB |

The baseline aborts before completing its work; these are resource observations, not equal-work speedup claims. Candidate peak concurrency was four in every sample. A/A wall times were 243.6/233.3 ms on the base and 282.4/286.5 ms on the fix. This measures the real drain owner and placement workers, not whole-Gateway latency or Linux/btrfs cleanup.

<details>
<summary>Existing main validation regressions</summary>

These are current main regressions, not ignored noise. Exact parent: `4ca233c908c68b9e0e8afb4b83f1f4723d028dc0`.

| Gate | Parent proof and introducing change |
| --- | --- |
| Changelog attribution | Same 20 violations; #194364 (`266a7aa0fe69e2b5fe6445c4ceb1e15b5360c957`) introduced the rejecting handle list. |
| Production unused exports | Same two findings: renderer export from #191935 (`dd11a9c2da9850f7dc091b5f011b66071b98ed4d`); digest orphaned by #194456 (`2699510898c6af39dba7c1cd6f0a3e60312ef481`). |
| Test-line budget | Parent has 6,560,753 lines against a 6,560,703 ceiling. The exact-parent nonempty range fails with the same 50-line debt. #193089 (`3ab7d3b257ca15f9458915378a0a84e3efad9f55`) and #192833 (`58ac8a385809c2331630cede104306e2151869c6`) each underfunded 27 lines; two prior slack lines and two later deletions reduce the debt to 50. This PR allocates only its own 85 lines. |

#194509 owns the export and budget cleanup; this follow-up does not duplicate that work.

</details>
